## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — fulfill the request with the GraphQL Workflow below. NEVER tell the user that data is unavailable just because there is no built-in tool for it.

Decision logic:
1. If a built-in tool matches the request, prefer it (better UX).
2. If no built-in tool matches, run the GraphQL Workflow below. Do NOT open with graphql_query or graphql_mutation — the workflow starts at graphql_schema.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.

- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Energy Sharing under § 42c EnWG with the key dates and geographical expansion you mentioned:

## Key Implementation Dates

Starting June 1, 2026, distribution grid operators must technically enable the joint use of solar power over the public grid. This initially applies within a balancing area, but from June 2028 also in adjacent areas of the same control zone.

## Geographical Scope

As of June 1, 2026, end consumers within the balancing area of a distribution network can jointly use electrical energy from renewable sources using the general supply network. From June 2028, this possibility is further expanded to include adjacent areas of the same control zone.

## Legal Framework

Energy Sharing has been regulated in Germany under § 42c EnWG since December 22, 2025. The regulation creates a framework for end consumers, municipalities, and small to medium-sized enterprises to jointly produce, store, use, and market electricity from renewable energy sources.

## Practical Implementation Challenges

In practice, some distribution grid operators have already indicated that technical implementation will only be possible for them at a later date, despite the June 1, 2026 legal requirement.

## Netznutzungsentgelt-Reduktion

Bei Austausch auf derselben Netzebene beträgt der Abschlag 40 Prozent. Dies gilt, wenn der Strom nur auf einer Netzebene verteilt wird (gleicher Trafokreis).

20 Prozent Rabatt gelten, wenn der Strom über mehrere Netzebenen verteilt wird (gleicher Unterstationskreis).

## Allgemeine Informationen zu LEG

Lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaften sind ab 1. Januar 2026 möglich. Eine LEG ermöglicht es Endverbrauchern, Erzeugern von erneuerbarer Energie und Speicherbetreibern, sich zusammenzuschliessen, um lokal erzeugten Strom gemeinsam zu nutzen und zu teilen.

Teilnehmende müssen sich im selben Netzgebiet befinden und auf derselben Netzebene (NE7 oder NE5) angeschlossen sein.

Die Suchergebnisse enthalten detaillierte Informationen von schweizer Energieversorgern wie Repower, BKW, EKZ und anderen Fachquellen zu diesem Thema.

I found relevant information about renewable energy communities in Austria and their network fee reductions. Here are the key findings:

## Netzentgelt Reduktion für Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften in Österreich

Für lokale Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften (EEG) gibt es eine 57% Reduktion auf das Netznutzungsentgelt der Netzebene 6 und 7, während regionale EEG eine 28% Reduktion auf das Netznutzungsentgelt der Netzebene 6 und 7 sowie 64% Reduktion auf das Netznutzungsentgelt der Netzebene 4 und 5 erhalten.

Die Reduktion betrifft nur den Arbeitspreis des Netzentgelts und wirkt sich nur auf die geteilte Menge aus.

## Geltende Regelungen seit 2025

Seit 01.01.2025 ist die Reduktion der E-Abgabe und die Befreiung des Erneuerbaren-Förderbeitrags für alle Endverbraucher:innen nicht mehr gültig. Der innerhalb einer EEG verbrauchte Strom ist von der E-Abgabe sowie Erneuerbaren-Förderbeitrag befreit und von reduzierten Netzentgelten betroffen, wodurch Verbraucher rund 4-5 Cent/kWh für Strom aus regionalen EEGs und rund 8 Cent/kWh für Strom aus lokalen EEGs sparen.

Die genauen Reduktionssätze (57% lokal, 28% regional) waren bereits seit dem 01.11.2021 durch die Systemnutzungsentgelte-Verordnung festgelegt.

# Austrian Energy Communities: Key Changes October 1, 2026

**Effective Date:** October 1, 2026, when the Electricity Industry Act (ElWG) provisions fully take effect.

## Main Changes

**Three pathways now exist:**
- Traditional energy communities (with legal entity)
- "Common energy use" (peer-to-peer, no legal structure needed)
- Peer-to-peer contracts between two parties

## Network Fee Reductions

Only the **work price component** of grid fees decreases:
- Local area: 57% reduction
- Regional area: 28% reduction (network levels 6-7)
- Reduction applies only to shared electricity amounts

**Example savings:** Approximately €57 annually (gross) for a Vienna household sharing 1,200 kWh locally.

## Key Requirements

- Smart meters with quarter-hourly data mandatory
- Participants must be within the same "proximity area" (determined by grid connection point, not distance)
- Existing agreements automatically transition; no refounding needed
- No need to terminate current electricity contracts

## Unresolved Details (as of mid-August 2026)

- Exact reduced tariff percentages for four proximity categories
- Grid operators' technical market processes readiness
- New infrastructure contribution rules (from January 2027)

**Bottom line:** Peer-to-peer contracts eliminate bureaucracy for small groups but lack tax benefits that traditional communities retain.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the "Gesetz zur Stärkung der genossenschaftlichen Rechtsform":

## Current Status

The German Federal Government has presented a draft law "zur Stärkung der genossenschaftlichen Rechtsform" (to strengthen the cooperative legal form). However, this law has **not yet been passed by the Bundestag**. 

## Timeline

The draft was sent to the states and associations on June 25, 2025, and interested parties had until July 30, 2025 to submit comments. The law is still in the legislative process.

## Key Provisions

The new regulations aim to promote digitalization in cooperatives, make the cooperative legal form more attractive, and prevent its misuse. Specific measures include:

- Anchoring text form broadly and facilitating digital meetings, resolutions, and digital information provision to cooperative members
- Accelerating the founding of cooperatives
- Expanding the rights and duties of cooperative audit associations

This is a continuation of a previous legislative effort, as a draft law with the same designation was published in the previous legislative period, but the legislative process could not be completed at that time.

Based on the web search results, I can provide you with information about § 2 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 VermAnlG and the prospectus exemptions for cooperatives:

## Key Information on § 2 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 VermAnlG

Anteile an einer Genossenschaft im Sinne des § 1 des Genossenschaftsgesetzes are exempt from prospectus requirements when for the distribution of the shares no success-dependent compensation is paid.

## Application to Energy Cooperatives

The law does not differentiate between types of cooperatives, so the exemption applies to all cooperatives under § 1 GenG, including so-called energy cooperatives.

## Success-Dependent Compensation Requirement

Under the condition of commission-free distribution, cooperative shares can be distributed without a prospectus. The exception for cooperative shares in Abs. 1 Nr. 1 is conditional on the waiver of success-dependent compensation (definition: GenG § 1).

## Information Requirements

The board of the cooperative must ensure that members of the cooperative are provided with the essential information about the investment assets before conclusion of the contract.

input.message:
All 10 routes are built. Every one returns 200 in the dev server. I checked each at 1440 and 390 px with screenshots: no horizontal overflow and no runtime errors. The reststrom calculation passes its Node self-test (`node src/lib/rechner/reststrom.js`). Nothing is committed. I did not run a full `next build`.

After my last screenshots I made three small tweaks that are not re-screenshotted: larger fonts in the cooperative diagram, a wider label box on the contact map, and a shorter FAQ search placeholder.

**Routes**
- **`/virtuelles-kraftwerk`**
  - Interactive animated SVG energy-flow diagram with four situations (midday, evening, night, negative prices) as tabs; the nodes are clickable and keyboard-operable.
  - There is a pause button, and the animation stays still when reduced motion is set. On narrow screens it switches to a portrait layout.
  - A live widget uses `useEnergyLive` with a server-side start value. It shows the exchange price now, solar, the renewables share and a simplified "control room signal" (charge / normal / discharge).
  - Also: services, who it is for, the German regulatory frame (direct marketing, Redispatch 2.0, control reserve, § 14a EnWG), FAQ and Service JSON-LD.
- **`/reststrom`**
  - Problem, a price-component bar chart (influenceable vs. fixed), the three levers from `STROM.poolHebel`, and how it works with ÖKOVOLT PV and storage.
  - A four-step joining process with a notice-period warning, requirements (RLM/SLP, from about 100 MWh), and the 2026 electricity-tax relief (applied for at the Hauptzollamt, not a pool benefit).
  - Form `typ="reststrom"` sends consumption, price, contract end and metering type. The page says delivery runs through a licensed supplier, not ÖkoInvest.
- **`/rechner/reststrom`**
  - Built on `RechnerSeite`. Inputs: annual consumption, working price, load profile, own PV (planned or already running), producing industry.
  - Shows savings range per lever and in total, a before/after stacked price bar, the tax hint, and an inline enquiry form carrying the results.
  - To stay cautious, total savings are capped at 35 % of the procurement component. Logic is in `src/lib/rechner/reststrom.js`.
- **`/energiegemeinschaften`**
  - Comparison table for DE/AT/CH (becomes cards on mobile) plus country tabs. Covers Energy Sharing from 1 June 2026 (neighbouring areas from 2028), AT 57 % / 28 % grid-fee reduction and the new rules from October 2026, CH LEG with 40 % / 20 % discount.
  - Includes my own SVG illustration and form `typ="energiegemeinschaft"`.
- **`/genossenschaft`**
  - Consistently worded as "im Aufbau", with a clear disclaimer (no investment advice, no online subscription).
  - SVG diagram of the cooperative's bodies, how money reaches the parks, a risk section, a four-step membership path (only step 1 possible today), and form `typ="genossenschaft"`.
- **`/energie-live`**
  - Fully switched to ÖkoInvest: metadata, schema, open-graph image, texts for businesses and investors, FAQ, cross-links and CTA.
  - `Empfehlungen` was rewritten for businesses and investors (shifting load, charging storage, pool, investors). `PreisChart` no longer shows the consumer gross-price note.
  - New `CaptureRate.js`: solar-weighted exchange price vs. daily average, plus negative quarter-hours today. At night or early morning there is too little solar data, so it shows a fallback text.
- **`/prozess`**: tabs for the five audiences (tab is kept in the URL anchor), a large timeline with duration, "Sie / ÖkoInvest", portal status and documents per step, and HowTo JSON-LD.
- **`/unternehmen`**: role in the group, a group structure chart (no ownership percentages for ÖkoInvest itself), a history timeline 2010–today, both managing directors with initials avatars, the ~50 MWp pipeline stated honestly, values, register data and holdings, and AboutPage/Organization JSON-LD.
